Emails Become A Member Our Mission The CENTER for Performing Arts at Rhinebeck is a 501(c)(3) not-for-profit organization that is dedicated, through its arts and education programs, to providing arts experiences for people of all ages, cultures, and backgrounds. The CENTER will: Maximize the use of its facility as a true community resource Design and/or develop complementary arts programs at area schools Provide opportunities for hands-on technical and performance training in all aspects of theatre arts leading toward presentation Assist in the development of individual and group performers by offering them the opportunity to benefit from The CENTER's facility, rich technical resources, and professional expertise. Inclusion / Diversity Statement: The CENTER for Performing Arts at Rhinebeck strives for diversity, inclusion, and equity as it is connected to our mission and critical to ensuring the well-being of our staff, volunteers, and the community we serve. We affirm the fundamental rights of all to feel valued and respected and embrace differences in gender, race, ethnicity, national origin, age, sexual orientation or identity, education, or disability that make our community rich. We are committed to growing an inclusive environment with equitable treatment for all, including a non-discriminatory, anti-racist approach, and providing equal opportunity for employment and advancement in all of our work. If you would like to join the conversation or have any thoughts or concerns, please e-mail us here. Accountability If you witness or experience ANY inappropriate discriminatory or harassing behavior at the CENTER, we encourage you to make your concerns known to lead production staff* or a member of RPAC's designated Accountability Panel. Production staff is obligated to pass on any complaints to a member of the Accountability Panel. It is that member’s mandated requirement to bring the issue to the attention of RPAC management for further investigation. RPAC management will maintain a record of all complaints. Upon receipt of a complaint, it is the responsibility of RPAC staff to investigate the matter, take appropriate and timely action, and keep the board of directors informed of incidents. All complaints of this nature will be handled with maximum confidentiality. We commit to producing and amplifying voices from underserved communities in our programming, and to seeking out, empowering, and creating safe spaces for those who have historically been marginalized or silenced. All Production Companies using The CENTER are obligated to honor this policy. Code of Conduct JoAnne Valentín Schubert , chairperson jvsmusicmom@gmail.com *Lead Production Staff refers to Musical and Stage Directors, Assistant Directors, Stage Managers, Assistant Stage Managers, and Producers who are 18 or older. **For more information or our full policy, please contact one of the committee member listed above. Accessibility. Barrier-Free Access: The theater has access for patrons using wheelchairs or walkers. On-grade entrances, elevators, railings, and wide doorways allow people to reach all areas of the theater. Designated parking spaces are conveniently located, and accessible restroom facilities are available.  The theatre has integrated seating for patrons in wheelchairs. Accessible Seating: Accessible seating is located in the first row of the theatre (where there are no steps). The best location for wheelchairs is in the first row. To better serve you, please call the box office or email us so we can reserve your best location. Please contact our Box Office in advance if you require special assistance of any kind, such as: Removal of a theatre seat to accommodate a wheelchair. Early admittance to the theatre; Assistance in getting to your seats. Please plan to arrive at least 30 minutes before curtain time so our staff may comfortably assist you to your seats. Assisted hearing devices: A listening system is available to patrons with hearing loss during all performances to assist them with amplification and clarity. The system makes use of lightweight headsets.  Patrons can sit anywhere in the theater and use headsets, which have adjustable volume controls. Headsets are available at the Box Office in the lobby prior to the performance. A major credit card or driver’s license is required as collateral. Financial Info. Emails Become A Member Register Our trained instructors teach Tap, Ballet, Pointe, Hip-Hop, Musical Theater, Acro, Lyrical, and Contemporary. We offer classes for ages 3 and up! CENTERstage Dance Studio is an Acrobatic Arts certified studio . Please read all of the following information and contact us with questions. CENTERstage Dance Studio offers a variety of levelled classes for ages 3-adult. We offer a fun environment with quality instruction. Our season follows the school year, with a new season beginning each September and concluding in May. We typically offer a summer session each year. Our 2024-2025 season is broken into three sessions: Session 1: September 9-November 1, 2024 Session 2: November 4, 2024- February 14, 2025 (no class 11/25-11/29; 12/23-1/3) Session 3: February 17- May 9, 2025 (no class 4/14-4/18) Recital Week: May 12-16; Recital Saturday May 17 Most of our classes perform at a recital in May, and though all students will learn the choreography, students are not required to perform in the recital. We accept new students during our summer session and during our first and second sessions during the school year season. We are not accepting new students to our classes in session 3. In this case, new student means a student who has not been enrolled since Session 2 of the season. We do not automatically enroll students.  Everyone must register for every session. GENERAL INFORMATION MONEY MATTERS A nonrefundable deposit is required to secure a spot in each class. We reserve the right to charge a transfer fee- please check your classes before registering! A payment plan is available each session. Registrants are responsible for keeping track of payment dates and for keeping their payment information current. A payment plan is available for the 2024-2025 season with the following schedule: For Session 1: $30 deposit due at registration, payment 1 on September 20, payment 2 on October 18. For Session 2: $30 deposit due at registration, payment 1 on November 18, payment 2 on December 2, Payment 3 on January 3. For Session 3: $30 deposit due at registration, payment 1 on March 7, payment 2 on April 4, Payment 3 on May 2. Registrations cancelled mid-session are not eligible for a refund.  We are not able to prorate tuition for late registrations. We offer two discount options: The Individual Unlimited Dance Pass is recommended for anyone registering for four or more hour long classes or five or more 45 minute classes in a session. You must choose this option when registering online. Registrants are encouraged to add up their class total to see if the Unlimited Pass is the better option for them. A 15% Multiperson Discount for family members who register at the same time. If applicable, the multiperson discount is applied automatically upon check out. Credit card payments can be taken online or over the phone. Note: Your payment may show up on your billing statement as ACT*RhinebeckPACENTER or ACT*RPA, Inc. If you wish to pay by CASH or CHECK, please call Victoria at 845-876-3088. Checks must be made out to RPA, Inc. RECITAL Our recital is planned for Saturday May 17, 2025 . If you choose to take part in the recital, there will be separate instructions sent regarding costume and shoe requirements. Please note that these requirements vary in cost. Please ask your dance instructor any recital gear questions. Summer session does not have a recital. POLICIES Students and parents/guardians must read and agree to our Studio Agreement before registering. Our classes are closed sessions. Adults should ask the instructor before entering the studios. In the event that a class must be canceled, we will attempt to get a substitute for that class.  If we cannot, we will schedule a makeup class when our schedule permits.  We try to keep makeup classes to a minimum. NOTE FOR PARENTS/GUARDIANS: We do not have the space for all adults and students to wait in our green room during classes. Participants only are permitted inside the theatre during classes. Parents/guardians are invited to wait in our parking lot or take advantage of the charms of the town of Rhinebeck. By registering your dancer, you are agreeing to this policy. PREDANCE PARENTS/GUARDIANS: Predance parents/guardians may wait in the green room but may not watch the class. By registering your dancer, you are agreeing to this policy. At this time, masks are optional but encouraged. All students that enter the theatre must sanitize their hands, and we ask anyone who is sick to please stay home. Please note that our policies can change at any time. Animals are not permitted in our theatre. Please note that we do not have reliable WiFi in our studio. Class Calendar and Registration Link We have adult classes! If the Beast does not learn his lesson soon, he and his household will be doomed for all eternity. Directed by Lynne Czajka. Kids on Stage is excited to present an abridged version of one of William Shakespeare's funniest plays, A Midsummer Night's Dream . Magic and mischief abound in this story of what happens when humans and fairies collide (sometimes literally!) in the forest.  The Fairy Queen and King are fighting, four young people are just trying to find love, and a group of workers are trying to put on a play. Approximately an hour long, this production is a wonderful introduction to Shakespeare or just a wonderful morning of live theatre! The Saturday Morning Family Series is made possible with support from Stewart’s Shops. At school, she’s bullied by the popular crowd, and virtually invisible to everyone else. At home, she's dominated by her loving but cruelly controlling mother. What none of them know is that Carrie’s just discovered she’s got a special power, and if pushed too far, she’s not afraid to use it.
